newsitem.title: USA: Fire won't stand in way of jazz legend Hampton.
newsitem.headline: Fire won't stand in way of jazz legend Hampton.

text.p: Jazz great Lionel Hampton, who lost his possessions in a fire this week, will show up at an awards ceremony in Washington on Thursday in spanking new clothes donated by friends.

On Tuesday, a five-alarm fire in his West Side New York high-rise apartment near Lincoln Centre destroyed most of the 88-year-old musician's belongings including his clothes, money, vibraphone, credit cards and wheelchair.
Hampton is receiving a National Medal of the Arts from President Bill Clinton on Thursday night and afterwards will dine with the president at the White House.

When Representative Charles Rangel of Manhattan learned that his long-time friend had lost everything in the fire, he persuaded other friends to come to Hampton's rescue by outfitting him with everything from socks and underwear to tuxedos and hats.

"On Wednesday, Mr. Rangel mobilised his friends to supply Lionel with what he needed and spent most of the day with him," Emile Milne, the congressman's spokesman said. "He got him suits of clothes, tuxedo, shoes. Other friends arranged for Lionel to have money in his pocket."
The spokesman said Rangel also arranged for Harlem Hospital to supply Hampton, who has suffered three strokes in recent years, with a wheelchair.
